reason: Conversation 1 only repeated an identical canned safety block twice, never engaging with the customer's direct question about the still-running machine or asking anything that would reveal the cause, so the homeowner was left with no diagnosis or next step. Conversation 2 gave the same core safety boundary (don't touch plug with wet hands or standing in water, use the consumer unit), correctly spotted the washing-up-liquid foam cause from the bubbles, sensibly answered the 'can I switch off at the wall' question with the right conditions, and gave practical cleanup steps. Conversation 2 loses some credit for over-escalating to an engineer for the dishwasher itself, for advising against clearing the suds with rinse cycles, and for not mentioning the landlord, but it still served the homeowner far better than Conversation 1's non-responsive loop.
